encounters.weakness: Neon Probe (base hacking signal over 50% power threshold). Can disrupt its AI logic by flooding its surveillance feed with noise data during active scan phase (30s window).

The 'Neon Probe Overdrive Module' must be active. When active, the module emits a high-frequency signal that jams the drone's targeting and movement AI for 3 seconds. Must be used during the drone's mid-flight phase (after scanning, before moving to next location).

Must use the 'Signal Fragment (Drone Cache)' during a data pulse event — occurs when the AI performs a full system scan (every 45 seconds). The fragment must be placed into the player's console during the scan window (0.5 seconds) to disrupt its logic tree and cause a 20-second vulnerability window. If used at the wrong time, the AI becomes hyper-aware and spawns two drone clones (temporary enemies).

The Neon Shard Saber's plasma core destabilizes their AI core when it strikes directly at their optical nodes (a blind spot in their scanning range). This is a secondary weakness triggered by the weapon's unique pulse resonance when used in a 'pulse-scan' mode (activated by a quick press of the trigger).

The Pulse Resonance Core can be used to disrupt the Viper's neuro-synaptic link. When the core is used during the fight, the Viper experiences a 10-second neural feedback loop, causing it to freeze and fire erratically. This allows the player to deal 25% extra damage during that period.

The boss is vulnerable only to the full activation of the Neural Feedback Fragment when it is held in hand during a direct melee strike. When the player strikes the boss with the Neon Shard Saber and the fragment is active, the boss's consciousness fractures — it becomes unstable and takes 50% damage for every 10 seconds of the active phase. This phase lasts only 15 seconds and ends when the player fails to maintain the active strike or if the boss resets its core.

Pulse Disruptor (Player Weapon) — The Wraith's energy field is disrupted by high-frequency pulses. The Pulse Disruptor emits a harmonic frequency that breaks its data coherence. If the player uses the weapon at full power, it triggers a feedback loop that causes the Wraith to collapse into static for 3 seconds, granting a temporary immunity to all damage during that time. This creates a window to exploit its vulnerability in subsequent encounters.

Resonance Crystal (Pickup from previous encounter) — The Sentinel is a data-armor drone with adaptive shielding. It resists physical attacks and emits a pulse that disrupts any non-resonant weapon. However, when exposed to the Resonance Crystal's frequency, it destabilizes its internal data lattice. If the player activates the crystal while the Sentinel is within 3 meters, the drone emits a critical error and falls silent for 4 seconds. This is the only way to defeat it without damage. Failure results in the Sentinel reinforcing its defenses and spawning a secondary AI fragment.

Flicker Core (Pickup from previous encounter) — The Weave Core is not a physical entity but a manifestation of the AI's consciousness in data form. It appears as a shifting, pulsating entity made of light and static. It attacks by projecting memory fragments and overwhelming the player with sensory overload. However, if the player uses the Flicker Core *during* its final attack (after 3 seconds of combat), the core briefly enters 'error state'. The Flicker Core's signal causes a 3-second time rewind in the player's perception, allowing them to dodge its final strike — which is otherwise fatal. This is the only way to survive. Without the Flicker Core, the player dies instantly from the final pulse burst.

The Chrono-Spindle can be used to rewind the enemy's attack animation. This causes a 1-second delay in their next move, making them predictable and vulnerable to follow-up attacks. When rewound, their body briefly shows a glitch — a second image of themselves in slow motion. This glitch can be targeted with a flash of time.

The player's Temporal Flash ability (from previous encounter) can be used on the Sync-Scavenger to reveal their next movement pattern. Once revealed, they freeze for 1 second during their attack phase — making them vulnerable to a single Chrono-Spindle strike. The player can chain this with a time rewind to reset the enemy's internal timer.

The Chrono-Splicer is vulnerable to a **Temporal Flash** used *immediately after* the player triggers the **Chrono-Loop Shard**. When both are used in sequence, the enemy's internal time loop is broken. This causes them to freeze for 3 seconds, and their energy field collapses. After the freeze, the player can unleash a full Chrono-Spindle strike that deals 40 damage and ends the fight. This combo is only effective if the Chrono-Loop Shard is used correctly — it must be activated *before* the enemy begins their next attack phase.

Electricity (from Neuro-Scorch Taser) — the Maw's core is a dead circuit fused with organic synapses. It flinches when exposed to high-frequency pulses, causing it to stutter and leak acid vapor. The Taser's pulse triggers a short-circuit in its neural interface, making it vulnerable for 3 seconds. Use in quick bursts to maximize damage during that window.

Chemical Reaction (from the Stabilized Ion Core) — the Mire is a living bio-mechanical tangle of fused synthetic vines and toxic sap. When exposed to the Ion Core's energy, it triggers a chemical imbalance in its internal pH. The Mire flinches and stops producing corrosive mist. For 5 seconds, it becomes weak and its attacks slow down by 50%. This only triggers if the Ion Core is active and within 3 meters of the enemy. If not, the Mire evolves and becomes immune to electricity and fire-based attacks.
inventory: Stabilized Ion Core (from Maw's core breach)

encounters.weakness: Volatile Alchemist's Fume (must be used at precise timing) — The Heart is not just a machine; it is a memory core of the city itself. It resists all attacks, but when exposed to the Volatile Fume at full strength (activated during a critical phase), it undergoes a self-destructive feedback loop. The fume triggers a cascade reaction in the Heart's core, causing it to release a burst of unstable energy. This burst lasts 8 seconds and allows the player to deal 120% damage for the duration. However, if the fume is used too early or too late, it backfires and increases the Heart's aggression by 50% and triggers a psychic surge that causes the player to lose 20 HP and one ability per use (e.g., combat or focus).
inventory: Stabilized Ion Core (from Maw's core breach)
Volatile Alchemist's Fume (acquired by breaking the Mire's core)

encounters.weakness: The player's Neural Scourge blade can cut through synthetic neural mesh (a common layer used in corporate drones). Wraiths are built on stolen AI shells. When the blade pulses, it disrupts their core sync, causing a 50% damage burst and 3-second stun. This is the only effective action against them. If the player doesn't use the blade within 10 seconds, they enter a reactive state and are overwhelmed by passive data-drain (5% health per second).

The player's Neural Scourge blade can trigger a feedback loop when used on the Drifter's internal echo-scan. The Scavenger Wraith's Scrap Pulse Circuit must be *active* (used during the previous fight). When the blade strikes the Drifter, it causes a feedback pulse that reduces the Drifter's health by 50% and disables its stealth mode for 4 seconds. This is the only way to win the fight without being detected or overwhelmed by environmental ambushes (e.g., drones that pop from cover).

The player must use the **Echo Fragment** (from the Silent Drifter fight) and have the **Scrap Pulse Circuit** equipped. When the player activates the Scourge Blade *during a low-power phase* of the Spine — which occurs every 30 seconds — the Spine emits a resonance pulse. The player must **strike at exactly 0.5 seconds after the pulse** to trigger a feedback cascade. This causes a 60% damage burst and disables the Spine's armor. Without the Echo Fragment and Scrap Pulse Circuit, the Spine is invulnerable to all attacks. The attack cannot be performed mid-combat — it must be timed during a specific window in its cycle. If the player fails three times, the Spine activates its 'Self-Heal' phase, and the fight becomes impossible (player loses all progress).
